MG-3.0 memory: every run so far

Matrix-Game 3.0 (distilled, 3 steps) on RunPod · LPIPS from the MIND mirror protocol and its pose-matched extension · built from whatever is on disk; anything not generated or scored yet is marked, never dropped silently

Overview1 · Outback (Oct 26)2 · Paper ablations, 40 s (Oct 26) 3 · Five tasks + overlays (Nov 17)4 · Five tasks × six ablations (Nov 18)5 · The other six ablations (Nov 18)

What the four runs say together

Interpretation across runs (all five runs complete)
  • MG-3.0's memory is real when the camera retraces its own path. Painting over the retrieved memory makes revisits worse in 47 of 48 retrace cells (run 3), and in the paper the no-memory ablation is clearly worse at long horizon (C1 0.507 vs C0 0.383). The model is looking things up, not just continuing the last frames.
  • It does not recognise a place reached by a different route. Loop back is the worst task by far (0.664 vs 0.29–0.42), and painting memory there changes nothing (5 of 12 up). Retrieval is driven by the commanded camera pose, so on a loop the right frames should be retrievable. The likely failure (not yet tested) is in using them from a new approach direction, or in pose drift around the loop, rather than in having no memory at all.
  • What sits in memory gets copied, faithfully. In the outback run (run 1), paint in memory and short-term context leaks straight into the image: half-painted context (b, c) washes the frame toward the paint colour or turns the painted half into a persistent flat floor. Painting long-term memory alone (a) keeps the picture sharp but changes what place it shows. Short-term context sets the look; long-term memory steers the content.
  • Single-clip rankings are noisy. On one 40 s clip (run 2), most conditions land between 0.48 and 0.65 and the order does not match the paper's 100-clip means (C8, worst in the paper, scores best here). Read run 2 for what each ablation looks like, and the paper and runs 3–4 for effects.
  • Run 4 pins down where the retrace memory sits: in the retrieved long-term frames. No memory (C1) and anchor-only memory (C2) are clearly worse. Random or spread slots cost little on simple out-and-back paths but a lot on midpath, where one particular place has to be found, so the frustum search matters for precise revisits. A shorter short-term window (C3) does not hurt. None of the six helps loop back, including the proposed spread-slot fix (C10), so loop back's failure is not about which frames sit in memory.
  • Run 5 changes the reading of loop back: at the end of the loop C0's memory already holds the right frames, yet the model does not redraw them. Only C4, which forces the start frame into the short-term context, scores well (0.26), and it does so by staying pinned to the start image. Loop back is a problem of using memory against conflicting recent context, not of retrieval. Content-similarity retrieval (C5) is clearly worse than frustum retrieval; 8 slots (C12) add little.

1 · Outback (2026-10-26)

condition C0 · 4 base images × 4 versions (original + memory overlays a, b, c from chunk 12, the walk back)

Path (same for every clip)
still 5s
walk out 15s
turn 180°
walk back 15s
777 frames at 17 fps (45.7 s), 19 chunks. W only, turn by mouse, ends at the origin. After the turn the camera looks at ground it never saw, so no frame on the walk back matches an earlier view: this run has no LPIPS (the only same-pose pairs are 29 frames inside the two still holds, which measure stillness, not memory). It is judged by eye.
Overlay variantsa: the 4 retrieved memory slots painted solid · b: right half, memory and short-term · c: bottom half, memory and short-term. Paint = the image's most common colour; the sink is never painted. Chunks 0–11 identical across versions.
What it shows (spiderverse checked frame by frame; the others agree by eye)
  • Original: the style drifts on the way back, from Spider-Verse comic shading to a flat blue look. With nothing on the walk back seen before, the model has only its memory of the outbound leg to hold style, and it slowly lets go.
  • a (memory painted solid): still sharp and coherent, but it becomes a different place. Long-term memory steers what is drawn, not image quality.
  • b (right half of memory + short-term painted): the whole image goes soft and washes toward the paint colour. Short-term context is copied almost directly into the next frames.
  • c (bottom half painted): the painted half turns into a flat floor that persists to the end. Once a wrong region sits in context, the model keeps it consistent rather than repairing it.
Takeaway: MG-3.0 trusts its context strongly. That is good for consistency on revisits (run 3) and bad when the context is wrong.

2 · Paper ablations on a 40 s loop (2026-10-26)

every condition from the paper (C0 to C11) · anchor data-25 · MIND path -w stretched to 8 chunks per leg (walk forward 19 s, walk backward 19 s)

How to read it
  • At 40 s, LPIPS saturates. The baseline C0 scores 0.549 here against 0.383 in the paper's k=4 average. Most conditions sit between 0.48 and 0.65, close enough that one clip cannot rank them.
  • Directions that agree with the paper: no long-term memory (C1 0.602), random slots (C6 0.637) and spread slots (C10 0.632) are all worse than C0, and 8 frustum slots (C11, flag C12, 0.478) is better.
  • Directions that don't: C8 (memory Plücker → identity) scores best here (0.436) but is worst in the paper's 100-clip mean (0.487). C7's camera stalls against a wall (motion 4.3), so its low 0.492 is flattered by near-static frames.
  • This is why runs 3 and 4 use 4 images × 5 tasks instead of one clip per condition.

Mirror LPIPS of this one clip per condition (paper scorer, shift −1, separation > 16, 311 pairs; C3 407), sorted. Hatched = camera motion under 6 (stalled, so LPIPS is flattered). Paper averages (short = k=1, 100 clips; long = k=4, 40 clips) are in the table.

3 · Five memory tasks with memory overlays (2026-11-17)

condition C0 · same 4 base images · 5 tasks × 4 versions (original + overlays a, b, c from chunk 9, the start of the revisit leg) · original and a/b/c share chunks 0–8 exactly

How LPIPS is scoredEach frame is compared with the earliest earlier frame at the same commanded pose, more than 16 frames before it. Mirror, L test and off-screen retrace themselves, so they use the paper's unchanged score_mirror.py; loop back and midpath use the pose-matched score_revisit.py (identical pairs on retracing paths). Lower = the model redrew what it showed before.
Read with careOne clip per cell, one seed. With 4 images per mean, gaps under ~0.05 are clip noise. A stalled camera scores well for the wrong reason, so check motion (mean frame-to-frame change, 0–255) in the tables.
What stood out (4 images, mean LPIPS of the original clip; lower = remembered)
  • Loop back is where memory fails: 0.664, against 0.41 for mirror and 0.42 for the L test. Coming back to the start by a different route, MG-3.0 does not redraw what was there, on every image (0.52–0.74).
  • On paths that retrace or revisit, painting over memory makes it worse almost every time: 47 of 48 image × overlay changes are higher LPIPS across mirror, midpath, L test and off-screen (the exception: spiderverse midpath with overlay a, −0.03), by +0.08 to +0.22 on average. So the model is using its retrieved memory there.
  • Loop back does not get worse with overlays (5 of 12 changes up, 7 down; mean change −0.01 to −0.09). Painting memory cannot hurt a scene the model was not recalling anyway.
  • Painting short-term context too (b, c) hurts more than painting memory alone (a): midpath +0.10 (a) vs +0.19 / +0.22 (b / c); off-screen +0.08 vs +0.13 / +0.15.
  • Turning away and back holds up: off-screen 0.364, better than walking out and back (0.408), though the held frames add easy pairs.
Caveats: midpath's 0.287 is the lowest, but ascii's camera stalls in the far half (0.085 there). Spiderverse barely moves on mirror (motion 2.8 vs 10–23), so its scores are flattered. Beach is the easiest image on every retrace task. n = 4 images, one seed each: gaps under ~0.05 are noise.

Dots = one base image each; bar = mean. Lower is better memory.

4 · The same five tasks under six ablations (2026-11-18)

C1 C2 C3 C6 C7 C10 against C0 (the originals of run 3: same seeds, same controls, so differences are the condition, not the noise draw) · 120/120 new clips scored · images complete: spiderverse, ascii, beach, forest · run order spiderverse → ascii → beach → forest · H100 80GB

What the six ablations say (mean LPIPS over the 4 images; Δ = change vs C0; lower = remembered)
  • Retrace memory lives in the retrieved long-term frames. Removing them (C1) is the worst condition on the retrace tasks: mirror +0.14, L test +0.11, off-screen +0.17, midpath +0.14, and worse than C0 in 15 of 16 image × task cells. Short-term context alone cannot bring the scene back.
  • The anchor frame alone is not enough either. C2 (every slot = the start frame) is next worst: +0.07 to +0.09 on the retrace tasks and +0.22 on midpath. The model needs frames from along the path, not just the start.
  • Which frames are retrieved matters most when the target is a specific place. Random slots (C6) and evenly spread slots (C10) cost little on mirror, L test and off-screen (+0.02 to +0.06): on those paths most of the past is the outbound leg, so almost any slot is useful. On midpath, which comes back to one particular stretch, they lose +0.15 and +0.12. The frustum search earns its keep there.
  • A shorter short-term window does not hurt revisits. C3 (1 latent instead of 4) is level with C0 or slightly better: mirror −0.00, off-screen −0.05, midpath −0.02, L test +0.04 (worse than C0 in only 8 of 16 cells). One reading is that less recent context puts more weight on retrieved memory. C3 also moves 52 frames per chunk, so this is not a clean single change.
  • C7 (no camera encoding) looks fine, but it isn't. Its LPIPS is close to C0 on mirror, L test and off-screen (midpath +0.08) because its camera barely moves (motion 2 to 8 against 9 to 23 for the others): without a pose signal the model under-moves, and near-static frames are easy to match. This is the paper's C7 caveat again.
  • Nothing fixes loop back. Every condition lands between 0.62 and 0.71 (C0 0.664). The small dips for C2 (−0.05) and C6 (−0.03) are within clip noise, and the proposed fix C10 is level (−0.02). Coming back by a different route fails whatever the memory holds or how it is picked.
Caveats: one seed, one clip per cell, n = 4 images per mean, so Δs under ~0.05 are noise. Spiderverse barely moves on mirror and midpath (motion ~3) in every condition, which flatters its scores. Its midpath C1 0.22 beating C0 0.42 is that, not a real gain.

Dots = one base image each; bar = mean over the images scored so far (n on hover); dashed = C0 mean over the same images. Lower is better memory.

Table view (mean LPIPS; Δ vs C0 over the same images)

5 · The other six ablations (2026-11-18)

C4 C5 C8 C9 C11 C12 against the same C0 (same seeds, same controls) · 120/120 clips scored · images complete: spiderverse, ascii, beach, forest · run order spiderverse → ascii → beach → forest

What the other six ablations say (mean LPIPS over the 4 images; Δ = change vs C0; lower = remembered)
  • C4 (recency killed) is the only condition that "solves" loop back, but not by remembering. Loop back drops from 0.664 to 0.258 (−0.41, on all four images). C4 puts the anchor (start) frame where the recent context should be, so every chunk is pulled toward the start image: its frames stay much closer to the first frame (travel 0.42 vs 0.65 for C0). Coming back to the start then matches almost by construction. On the other tasks it is mixed (L test −0.05, off-screen +0.05, midpath +0.06).
  • Loop back fails in how the model uses memory, not in what it retrieves. On the re-walked first side (chunks 15–16), C0's memory already holds the right frames (62–110, the first side) on all four images, yet it scores 0.66. When the start view is in the short-term context instead (C4), the model redraws it. Hypothesis, not yet tested: when memory slots and recent context disagree, the model follows the recent context.
  • Retrieving by content similarity is worse than retrieving by camera frustum. C5 is the worst condition of this run: +0.05 to +0.16 on every retrace task, worse than C0 in 14 of 16 cells.
  • More slots do not help much; more spread slots hurt. 8 frustum slots (C12) are level with C0 on the retrace tasks (−0.01 to +0.01) and only slightly better on loop back (−0.04). 8 evenly spread slots (C11) are worse on mirror, L test and midpath (+0.06 to +0.14), better on off-screen (−0.04) and loop back (0.559, −0.11).
  • Dedup retrieval (C9) and memory pose → identity (C8) change little on these tasks (−0.02 to +0.07). C8 being near-level is surprising, since it is the worst condition in the paper's 100-clip average (0.487 at k=1).
Caveats: one seed, n = 4 images per mean. This run mixed H100 and A100 pods, and the same seed gives a different clip on each (0.448 vs 0.412 on one test clip), so Δs under ~0.05 are noise. Motion is comparable across conditions here (10–14), so none of these scores is flattered by a stalled camera.

Dots = one base image each; bar = mean over the images scored so far (n on hover); dashed = C0 mean over the same images. Lower is better memory.
